note: Public activity cards only. Private house notes stripped. Affiliate query params removed. First id wins.

curated.title: Electric Bike Tour of Bend & Deschutes River
curated.description: Explore Bend and the Deschutes River with ease on a guided e-bike tour. With an electric bike to assist, you can go farther and see more while learning local history and stopping for refreshments.
curated.tip: Includes e-bike and helmet; wear closed-toe shoes.
curated.imageAlt: An electric bicycle and another rider in a bike lane in Bend

curated.title: Ride the River Guided E-Bike Tour of Bend
curated.description: A relaxed guided e-bike ride focusing on Bend's riverfront, Old Mill District, and neighborhood highlights — great for visitors who want a local introduction.
curated.tip: Smaller groups sell out on weekends; book ahead.
curated.imageAlt: Riders on e-bikes following a river path

curated.title: Deschutes River E-Bike Tour
curated.description: A shorter e-bike experience focused on scenic stretches of the Deschutes River and nearby attractions — ideal for casual riders.
curated.tip: Bring a water bottle and camera for river views.
curated.imageAlt: E-bike parked near a river bank

curated.title: Cascade Lakes Kayak Tour
curated.description: Guided kayak tours among the Cascade Lakes — stunning alpine scenery and calm water paddling. Some itineraries include multiple lakes and shore snacks.
curated.tip: Dress in layers; water can be chilly even on warm days.
curated.imageAlt: Kayaks on a calm mountain lake

curated.title: 2-Hour High Cascades Scenic ATV Tour
curated.description: Off-road ATV rides through High Cascades terrain — fast-paced, scenic fun with guided instruction and safety gear provided.
curated.tip: Closed-toe shoes required; bring sun protection and gloves if you have them.
curated.imageAlt: ATV riding on volcanic terrain

curated.title: Deschutes River Horse Ride
curated.description: Guided horseback rides along the Deschutes River corridor — serene river views and a relaxed pace suitable for most riders.
curated.tip: Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes; bring a camera for riverside views.
curated.imageAlt: Horseback rider trotting along a riverside trail

curated.title: Cascade Lakes Moonlight & Starlight Canoe Tour
curated.description: A guided evening canoe tour under the stars — magical moonlit paddling with storytelling and light refreshments.
curated.tip: Check moon phase and weather; tours run on calm nights.
curated.imageAlt: Canoes on a lake at night under a starry sky

curated.title: Guided Lava Tube Cave Tour
curated.description: Naturalist-led exploration of local lava tubes — learn volcanic geology and see dramatic subterranean formations. Guides provide lights and helmets.
curated.tip: Wear warm layers and sturdy shoes; tours often require bending and uneven footing.
curated.imageAlt: Inside a lava tube cave with a guided group

curated.title: Limited-Entry Lava Tube Cave Tour
curated.description: Smaller-group or limited-access lava tube experiences — often include expert-led interpretation and quieter cave sections.
curated.tip: Limited-entry tours may require advance booking and have minimum fitness levels.
curated.imageAlt: Tour group inside a narrow lava tube

curated.title: Alpaca Picnic Experience
curated.description: Meet alpacas and enjoy a guided outdoor picnic — a family-friendly experience combining animal encounter and local snacks.
curated.tip: Perfect for kids and small groups — book for a private time slot.
curated.imageAlt: Picnic with alpacas in a meadow

curated.title: Chocolate Tour (Hot Chocolate & Samples)
curated.description: A tasty guided walk sampling chocolate, hot cocoa, and paired treats at local shops — a sweet local introduction.
curated.tip: Great as a half-day indulgence — bring comfortable shoes.
curated.imageAlt: Assorted chocolates and hot chocolate cups

curated.title: Food Truck & Brewery Tour (Complimentary Tastings)
curated.description: A guided tasting tour pairing Bend's food-truck scene with local breweries — small-group format with curated tastings.
curated.tip: Designated driver or transportation recommended when sampling beers.
curated.imageAlt: Assortment of food truck dishes and craft beer

curated.title: Craft Brewery Tour with Tastings
curated.description: A curated brewery crawl showcasing Bend's best craft beer scene with guided tastings and behind-the-scenes insights.
curated.tip: Bring ID; tours often include transportation between stops.
curated.imageAlt: Tasting flight of craft beers

curated.title: Ultimate Scavenger Bend (Downtown)
curated.description: A playful city-wide scavenger hunt exploring downtown Bend's history, public art, and hidden gems — great for groups.
curated.tip: Works well for team outings or family groups; wear comfortable shoes.
curated.imageAlt: Group solving clues in a downtown setting

curated.title: Central Oregon Night Sky Photo Tour
curated.description: A guided astrophotography outing to prime dark-sky locations with instruction on long-exposure techniques — capture the Milky Way over the Cascades.
curated.tip: Bring a tripod and spare batteries; instructors often provide remote triggers.
curated.imageAlt: Starry Milky Way over a mountain silhouette

curated.title: Personal Photography Tutoring in Bend
curated.description: One-on-one or small-group photography tutoring focused on composition, camera settings, and local shooting locations.
curated.tip: Share your gear and learning goals when booking for a tailored session.
curated.imageAlt: Photographer leading a tutoring session outdoors

curated.title: Private Bend Street Photo Tours
curated.description: Private guided street photography tours through Bend's most photogenic neighborhoods and the Old Mill District — great for aspiring photographers and visitors who want curated shots.
curated.tip: Book a morning slot for softer light and fewer people.
curated.imageAlt: Photographer shooting in an urban streetscape

curated.title: Small-Group Paddle Board & Happy Hour — Cascade Lakes
curated.description: Paddle boarding on calm waters followed by a lakeside happy hour — a relaxed small-group outing on the Cascade Lakes.
curated.tip: Bring swimwear and a towel; tours often include light snacks.
curated.imageAlt: Paddle boards lined up on a lake shore

curated.title: Murder Mystery Detective Experience
curated.description: An interactive city-based murder-mystery experience — team up, solve clues, and explore Bend in a playful way.
curated.tip: Fun for groups — good for rainy-day entertainment.
curated.imageAlt: Clues and map on a table for a detective game

curated.title: Hot Lava Bakery
curated.description: Fresh pastries, croissants, and coffee in Sunriver Village — a local favorite for breakfast and take-away treats.
curated.distance: 5 min by bike to the Village
curated.tip: Arrive before 9:30 AM in peak season.
curated.imageAlt: Fresh pastries and croissants in a bakery display

curated.title: Sparrow Bakery
curated.description: Bend's cult-favorite bakery famous for the ocean roll — a buttery, salted-sweet masterpiece. Also excellent savory pastries and coffee.
curated.tip: Ocean rolls sell out — go early or pre-order.
curated.imageAlt: Fresh baked goods on a counter

curated.title: Rio Sol at Sunriver Marina
curated.description: Latin American cuisine and craft cocktails on the Deschutes River at the Sunriver Marina. Scenic sunset dinners with water views.
curated.tip: Request a patio table for golden-hour views.
curated.imageAlt: Outdoor dining with river views at sunset

curated.title: El Caporal
curated.description: Authentic Mexican cuisine with lively margaritas and a warm Village atmosphere.
curated.distance: 5 min by bike to the Village
curated.tip: Try the carne asada tacos and house margaritas.
curated.imageAlt: Mexican dish with tortillas and salsa

curated.title: Blondie's Pizza
curated.description: Wood-fired, family-friendly pizza in Sunriver — great for groups and takeout.
curated.tip: Order ahead on busy summer nights.
curated.imageAlt: Wood-fired pizza fresh from the oven

curated.title: Village Bar & Grill
curated.description: Casual American fare, cocktails, and a friendly local vibe right in the Village.
curated.tip: Good spot for families and late-night bites.
curated.imageAlt: Bar and grill dining area with rustic decor

curated.title: The Wallow
curated.description: Contemporary Pacific Northwest dishes with seasonal ingredients and a refined yet relaxed dining room.
curated.tip: Excellent for date nights and special occasions.
curated.imageAlt: Elegant plated entree on a table

curated.title: Campfire Cucina
curated.description: Italian-inspired cooking with wood-fired flavors — pizza, pasta, and shareable small plates.
curated.tip: Great for groups — try a few small plates to share.
curated.imageAlt: Pasta and Italian dishes on a wooden table

curated.title: Century Common Taps & Trucks
curated.description: A rotating lineup of food trucks paired with local craft taps — casual outdoor dining and community vibes.
curated.tip: Check the events calendar for truck lineups and tap takeovers.
curated.imageAlt: Outdoor food trucks and beer taps

curated.title: Josie K's Deli
curated.description: Casual deli fare with hearty sandwiches, salads, and quick grab-and-go options for day trips.
curated.tip: Perfect for picnic boxes and quick lunches.
curated.imageAlt: Deli sandwich on a plate

curated.title: Benham Falls
curated.description: The largest waterfall on the upper Deschutes River, thundering through a rugged lava canyon. Mostly flat, family-friendly, and beautiful year-round.
curated.seasonLabel: Best in spring for peak flow
curated.tip: Combine with a bike ride on the Deschutes River Trail.
curated.imageAlt: Waterfall cascading through a forest canyon
curated.gettingThere: Short drive or bike ride from Sunriver. Trailhead parking off Forest Road 41.

curated.title: Deschutes River Trail
curated.description: Paved and dirt paths following the Deschutes River through pine forest. Walk or bike from Sunriver toward Benham Falls.
curated.tip: Flat and scenic — perfect for an evening stroll.
curated.imageAlt: Dirt trail beside the Deschutes River on the way to Benham Falls

curated.title: Smith Rock State Park
curated.description: Oregon's most iconic crags — golden cliffs rising above the Crooked River. Misery Ridge is the classic loop with jaw-dropping views. Also world-class rock climbing.
curated.tip: Start early — the trail gets hot and crowded by midday in summer.
curated.imageAlt: Dramatic rocky cliffs and river canyon

curated.title: Green Lakes Trail
curated.description: A Central Oregon classic — hike through wildflower meadows and lava fields to impossibly blue alpine lakes beneath the South Sister volcano.
curated.tip: Arrive before 7 AM on weekends — the trailhead fills fast. Start early and bring layers — elevation gain and afternoon storms are real.
curated.imageAlt: Alpine lake surrounded by mountain peaks
curated.gettingThere: 45 min drive to trailhead off Cascade Lakes Highway.

curated.title: Todd Lake Loop
curated.description: Alpine lake loop at 6,500 ft with wildflowers in summer and Mt. Bachelor views. Cool escape on hot days.
curated.tip: Arrive early — small parking lot fills quickly on weekends.
curated.imageAlt: Todd Lake with Mount Bachelor behind it in the Deschutes National Forest

imageCredit.author: U.S. Forest Service, Pacific Northwest Region

curated.gettingThere: 25 min drive up Cascade Lakes Highway from Mt. Bachelor turnoff.

curated.title: Tam McArthur Rim
curated.description: A relatively short hike with enormous payoff — stand on the rim of a glacial cirque with views of Broken Top, the Three Sisters, and endless Cascades.
curated.tip: Wildflowers peak in July. Bring layers — it's exposed at the top.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain ridge trail with panoramic views

curated.title: Tumalo Falls
curated.description: A 97-foot waterfall just outside Bend with a scenic loop trail above the falls. Easy access and one of the most photographed spots in Central Oregon.
curated.seasonLabel: Year-round — check road access in winter
curated.tip: The upper trail gives you views most visitors miss.
curated.imageAlt: Tall waterfall in a lush forest

curated.title: Lava Butte & Lava Lands
curated.description: Climb a cinder cone for 360° views of volcanic landscape, then walk the paved Lava Lands loop through jagged black lava fields. Great for all ages.
curated.tip: Timed entry may be required in summer — check recreation.gov. Combine with the Lava River Cave or Lava Cast Forest for a full volcanic day.
curated.imageAlt: Lava Butte cinder cone with volcanic landscape
curated.trailDistance: Lava Butte 1.5 miles round trip; Lava Lands Trail 0.5 miles
curated.gettingThere: 10 min drive to Lava Lands Visitor Center. May require a timed entry pass in summer.

curated.title: SHARC Aquatic Center
curated.description: Sunriver's premier aquatic center — waterslides, lazy river, lap pool, surf simulator, rock climbing wall, and fitness center. Your stay includes 8 guest passes.
curated.imageAlt: Outdoor swimming pool with water slides

curated.title: Elk Lake
curated.description: A gorgeous alpine lake at 4,900 ft with sandy beaches, paddle rentals, and Mt. Bachelor as a backdrop. The water is cold but refreshing on hot summer days.
curated.tip: Grab lunch at the Elk Lake Resort cafe on the shore.
curated.imageAlt: Clear alpine lake with pine trees and mountains

curated.title: Sparks Lake
curated.description: One of the most photographed lakes in Oregon — shallow, crystal-clear water with South Sister reflected on calm mornings. Wade in from the shore or bring a float.
curated.tip: Sunrise here is magical — bring a camera.
curated.imageAlt: Serene lake reflecting mountain peaks at sunrise

curated.title: Paulina Lake
curated.description: A deep volcanic lake inside the Newberry Caldera with hot springs on the far shore, boat rentals, and excellent fishing. Two lakes in one caldera — East Lake is nearby.
curated.tip: Hike to Paulina Peak for a caldera overview before swimming.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain lake with forest shoreline

curated.title: Devil's Lake
curated.description: A pristine alpine lake tucked in a glacial cirque with stunning mountain views and excellent swimming. Crystal-clear water and a scenic trail loop make it a must-visit destination.
curated.tip: Arrive early — parking fills quickly on weekends.
curated.imageAlt: Alpine lake surrounded by forested mountains

curated.title: Eaglewood Community Pool
curated.description: Eaglewood Community Pool in Central Oregon.
curated.tip: Check the HOA board by the pool for seasonal hours.
curated.imageAlt: Community swimming pool on a sunny day

curated.title: Deschutes River Float
curated.description: The quintessential Central Oregon summer experience — float the gentle Deschutes on a tube or kayak through pine forests. Popular routes run from Sunriver toward Bend.
curated.tip: Rent tubes at the Sunriver Marina or in Bend. Bring sunscreen and a dry bag.
curated.imageAlt: Kayaking on a calm river through forest

curated.title: Sun Country Tours Whitewater
curated.description: Guided rafting trips on the Deschutes — from mellow scenic floats to Class III rapids through Big Eddy. Professional guides, all gear included.
curated.distance: Pickup in Bend or Sunriver area
curated.tip: Book the Big Eddy Thriller for families with teens.
curated.imageAlt: Whitewater raft navigating river rapids

curated.title: Big Eddy Thriller
curated.description: The Deschutes' most famous whitewater stretch — Class III rapids through a scenic canyon. Half-day guided trips suitable for adventurous beginners.
curated.tip: Wear a swimsuit under the wetsuit — you'll get soaked.
curated.imageAlt: Raft going through whitewater rapids

curated.title: Deschutes River SUP & Kayak
curated.description: Calmer sections of the Deschutes near Sunriver are perfect for stand-up paddleboarding and kayak exploring. Several outfitters rent gear by the half-day.
curated.tip: Morning water is glassy — best for SUP.
curated.imageAlt: Stand-up paddleboarding on a calm lake

curated.title: Mt. Bachelor Ski Resort
curated.description: 3,365 acres of lift-served terrain on a single volcano — groomers, bowls, glades, and a legendary spring skiing season that runs into May. 24 minutes from the house.
curated.tip: Buy lift tickets online in advance during peak weeks.
curated.imageAlt: Skier carving down a snowy mountain slope

curated.title: Mt. Bachelor Nordic Center
curated.description: 56 km of groomed cross-country trails through snow-covered forests at the base of the volcano. Rentals and lessons available for all skill levels.
curated.tip: The Twilight Trail is magical under the lights.
curated.imageAlt: Cross-country skier on a snowy forest trail

curated.title: Hoodoo Ski Area
curated.description: A fun, family-friendly ski area on Santiam Pass with night skiing, affordable tickets, and a laid-back vibe. Smaller than Bachelor but less crowded.
curated.tip: Night skiing on weekends is a unique experience.
curated.imageAlt: Snowboarder on a mountain with pine trees

curated.title: Mt. Bachelor Scenic Chairlift
curated.description: Not just for winter — ride the Pine Marten lift in summer for hiking, mountain biking, and panoramic views from 9,000 ft. Cool escape on hot days.
curated.tip: Bring a jacket — it's 20° cooler at the top.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain summit view above the clouds

curated.title: Phil's Trail Complex
curated.description: Bend's most beloved trail network — flowing singletrack through ponderosa pine with options from mellow to technical. Dozens of interconnected loops.
curated.tip: Start with 'Phil's Trail' proper — the original and still the best intro.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain biker on a forest trail

curated.title: Wanoga Snow Park Trails
curated.description: In winter, this sno-park transforms into fat-bike and cross-country ski terrain. In summer, nearby trails like Swampy Lakes offer high-elevation riding.
curated.tip: Check Trailforks for current trail conditions before heading out.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain biker riding through a pine forest

curated.title: Mt. Bachelor Bike Park
curated.description: Lift-served downhill mountain biking in summer — no pedaling uphill required. Trails from green to double-black with full-suspension rentals at the base.
curated.tip: Rent a downhill bike at the base — it's worth it.
curated.imageAlt: Downhill mountain biker on a forest trail

curated.title: Sunriver Paved Path Network
curated.description: Sunriver Paved Path Network in Central Oregon.
curated.tip: Ride to the Village for breakfast, then loop back via the river trail.
curated.imageAlt: Family biking on a paved path through trees

curated.title: Tiddlywinks & Forest Service Trails
curated.description: Playful, berm-filled flow trails near Bend that feel like a roller coaster on two wheels. Popular with intermediate riders looking for fun, not suffering.
curated.tip: Ride mid-week to avoid crowds.
curated.imageAlt: Mountain biker navigating a berm on a flow trail

curated.title: Crater Lake National Park
curated.description: The deepest lake in the US, filling a collapsed volcano caldera with impossibly blue water. Rim Drive, boat tours to Wizard Island, and hikes for every ability.
curated.tip: Enter from the north entrance for the shortest drive from Sunriver.
curated.imageAlt: Crater Lake with deep blue water and volcanic rim

curated.title: Lava River Cave
curated.description: Explore a mile-long lava tube — bring flashlights and warm layers for this underground adventure. One of the longest lava tubes in Oregon.
curated.tip: Rent lanterns at the entrance — phone flashlights aren't enough.
curated.imageAlt: Dark cave tunnel with light at the end

curated.title: High Desert Museum
curated.description: World-class museum blending live wildlife, Oregon history, and art. Otters, raptors, a 1904 homestead, and immersive exhibits — great for rainy days or mid-day heat.
curated.tip: Allow at least 3 hours — there's a lot to see.
curated.imageAlt: Natural history museum exhibit with wildlife

curated.title: Newberry National Volcanic Monument
curated.description: A massive shield volcano with obsidian flows, Paulina Falls, hot springs, and two crater lakes. Central Oregon's volcanic heart.
curated.tip: Stop at Paulina Falls on the way in — a quick, rewarding hike.
curated.imageAlt: Volcanic landscape with lake and forest

curated.title: Sunriver Stargazing
curated.description: Sunriver Stargazing in Central Oregon.
curated.tip: New moon weeks are best. Turn off deck lights for 10 minutes.
curated.imageAlt: Starry night sky over a dark landscape

curated.title: Woodlands Golf Course
curated.description: Woodlands Golf Course in Central Oregon.
curated.tip: McDivot's Cafe at the clubhouse is perfect for a post-round drink.
curated.imageAlt: Golf course fairway lined with pine trees

curated.title: Crosswater Club
curated.description: A world-renowned golf course designed by Peter Jacobsen and Jim Hardy — two courses ranked among the best in the Pacific Northwest. Public tee times available.
curated.tip: Book well ahead — this is a bucket-list course.
curated.imageAlt: Scenic golf course with mountain backdrop

curated.title: Sunriver Stables
curated.description: Guided trail rides through the pines for all experience levels, plus pony rides for little ones. A memorable family outing in any season.
curated.tip: Book the sunset ride for golden light through the trees.
curated.imageAlt: Horseback riding on a forest trail

curated.title: The Village at Sunriver
curated.description: The heart of Sunriver — shops, restaurants, an ice rink in winter, live music in summer, and events year-round. A five-minute bike ride from the house.
curated.tip: Check the events calendar for concerts and festivals.
curated.imageAlt: Forest village with shops and pathways
